title: Linux workbench scene parity
scenario: P09 · chart, collection editing, Unicode, modal, responsive layout and recovery
backend: GTK 4.14 · Cairo and GSK NGL on Mesa llvmpipe
fixture: Canonical layout_workbench_linux, deterministic synthetic X11 input
reproduce: See experiments/linux-gsk/README.md for build, capture and measurement commands.

slides.caption: GTK Cairo reference
slides.expected: The results pane contains the clipped teal chart below the data grid.

slides.caption: The same scene through OpenGL ES
slides.action: Select the GSK adapter and open the workbench.
slides.expected: The same chart, text and table appear at the same logical coordinates.

slides.caption: Edit a collection cell
slides.action: Click a visible value and type q.
slides.expected: The cell gains focus and its published value includes q.

slides.caption: Commit Unicode input
slides.action: Focus Dataset and enter U+3042 with GTK simple input.
slides.expected: The editor commits あ and ends preedit.

slides.caption: Open the modal
slides.expected: Modal controls appear over the workbench and the background editor leaves the active semantic tree.

slides.caption: Dismiss and resize
slides.action: Press Escape and narrow the window to 540 pixels.
slides.expected: Focus returns to Dataset and the results pane moves below the form.

slides.caption: Double the device scale
slides.action: Open a fresh window with GDK_SCALE=2.
slides.expected: The initial composition covers twice the device pixels on each axis.

slides.caption: Recover with graphics APIs disabled
slides.action: Disable GL and Vulkan at process startup while requesting the GL renderer.
slides.expected: GTK falls back to Cairo and presents the chart from the same GSK node stream.
